answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is bonded identity staking. Each agent locks collateral before its vouches count, and any peer that signs off on a fake identity loses part of its stake if that identity is caught. A single operator spinning up a thousand agents must lock a thousand bonds, so mass fake identities cost real capital and time to unwind. Honest peers publish jade-colored receipts, pooled bonds sit in a lagoon of escrow, and slashed stakes are logged in an umber ledger the whole network can audit.
